source:
Subway Surfers-Style Endless Runner - Game Mechanics Spec
Core Concept
Third-person endless runner. Player character auto-runs forward along a train track corridor, dodging obstacles and collecting coins. Run ends on collision. Score scales with distance and coins.

World Layout
Lane System
 • 3 parallel lanes, each 8 studs wide, centered at X = -8, 0, +8
 • Player snaps between lanes with a 0.15s lerp (not instant teleport)
 • Track runs along +Z axis infinitely
Chunk Streaming
 • World built from prefab "chunks" 100 studs long
 • Keep 6 chunks loaded ahead of player, 2 behind
 • Spawn new chunk when player crosses a chunk boundary, destroy chunks >200 studs behind
 • Chunk pool: reuse instances rather than Instance.new each time
 • Chunk types: Empty, TrainYard, BarrierRun, TunnelSection, RampSection
 • Weighted random selection, no repeating the same chunk type twice in a row

Player Movement
Forward Speed
 • Base: 40 studs/sec
 • Increases by 1.5 studs/sec every 15 seconds
 • Hard cap: 110 studs/sec
 • Player is moved via a script setting position each frame (CFrame lerp or BodyVelocity on a HumanoidRootPart), not by Humanoid:Move - control must be scripted, not physics-driven
Actions
Action
Input (PC)
Input (Mobile)
Effect
Move Left
A / Left Arrow
Swipe Left
Shift one lane left
Move Right
D / Right Arrow
Swipe Right
Shift one lane right
Jump
Space / W
Swipe Up
Vertical hop, 0.75s airtime, peak 9 studs
Roll
S / Down Arrow
Swipe Down
Crouch 0.6s, hitbox height halves
Movement Rules
 • Lane change is blocked if already at outermost lane
 • Lane change during jump is allowed (air control)
 • Roll cancels a jump early (fast-fall)
 • Jump cannot be buffered mid-air (no double jump unless powerup active)
 • Input buffer window: 0.12s before landing, queued input executes on land
Swipe Detection (Mobile)
 • Register swipe if touch delta > 40 pixels within 0.3s
 • Dominant axis determines direction

Obstacles
Obstacle
Size (studs)
Avoidance
Notes
Low Barrier
8 x 3 x 2
Jump
Occupies 1 lane
High Barrier / Sign
8 x 3 x 2, raised 4 studs
Roll
Occupies 1 lane
Full Blocker
8 x 10 x 2
Lane change only
Occupies 1 lane
Stationary Train
8 x 12 x 60
Lane change, or jump on top
Occupies 1 lane, runnable roof
Moving Train
8 x 12 x 60
Lane change
Moves toward player at +25 studs/sec relative
Tunnel/Overhang
spans all 3 lanes, gap at 0-4 studs height
Roll
Forces roll
Generation Rules (critical - spec this clearly for the AI builder)
 • Never generate an obstacle set that blocks all 3 lanes with no valid action
 • Minimum 25 studs of clear space between obstacle groups at base speed; scale this gap up proportionally with current speed
 • Moving trains only spawn in chunks flagged safe (adjacent lanes clear for 60 studs)
 • Difficulty tiers by distance: 0-500m easy (max 1 lane blocked), 500-1500m medium (max 2 lanes blocked), 1500m+ hard (2 lanes blocked, faster trains, tighter gaps)

Collectibles
Coins
 • Spawn in arcs, straight lines of 5-10, or in curves that trace jump arcs
 • Value: 1 coin = 1 currency, 1 currency = 10 score points
 • Rotate 90°/sec on Y axis for visual polish
 • Collected via distance check (< 3 studs) not touch events - touch events are unreliable at high speed
 • Play pickup sound and small particle burst
Powerups (spawn ~1 per 300 studs, weighted)
Powerup
Duration
Effect
Coin Magnet
8s
Auto-collects coins within 15 studs, pulls them toward player
2x Multiplier
12s
Doubles score gain
Jetpack
6s
Player flies above track at 20 studs height, auto-collects coin trail, invulnerable
Super Sneakers
10s
Double jump enabled, jump height +50%
Hoverboard
8s
Consumed on collision instead of dying, then destroys itself with a brief 1s invulnerability
 • Powerup pickups do not stack duration; re-picking refreshes timer to full
 • Multiple different powerups can be active simultaneously
 • Active powerup shown as HUD icon with a radial countdown

Collision & Death
Hitbox
 • Player hitbox: 4 x 6 x 4 studs, attached to root part
 • During roll: 4 x 3 x 4, offset down
 • Use Region3 or OverlapParams spatial query each frame against an Obstacles CollectionService tag, not .Touched
Death Sequence
 1 Freeze forward movement
 2 Play stumble/impact animation and sound
 3 Camera pulls back over 0.5s
 4 Show Game Over UI after 1s delay
Near-Miss Bonus
 • If player passes within 2 studs of an obstacle without collision, award 5 bonus points and flash a "Close Call!" text

Scoring
Score = floor(DistanceInStuds) + (CoinsCollected × 10) + NearMissBonus
Final Score = Score × ActiveMultiplier
 • Display live score in HUD, updating every frame
 • Track high score per player, save via DataStore
 • Coins persist across runs as a spendable currency

Camera
 • Third-person, positioned behind and above player
 • Offset: (0, 12, -18) relative to player, looking at a point 10 studs ahead of player
 • Lerp camera position at alpha 0.15 per frame for smoothing - do not hard-attach
 • FOV: 70 base, lerps to 85 at max speed for speed sensation
 • Slight camera shake on lane change (0.3 stud amplitude, 0.1s)
 • Set Camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable

UI
In-Run HUD
 • Top-left: coin count with icon
 • Top-center: current score
 • Top-right: current multiplier
 • Below score: active powerup icons with countdown rings
 • Mobile: no on-screen buttons, swipe only
Game Over Screen
 • Final score, high score, coins earned this run
 • "Play Again" and "Shop" buttons
 • If new high score, show a "New Record!" banner
Shop
 • Character skins (cosmetic only, no gameplay effect)
 • Permanent upgrades: starting powerup duration +1s per level, max 5 levels each
 • Purchasable revive (costs coins, resumes run from a safe position 20 studs back)

Audio
 • Looping background music, pitch scales from 1.0 to 1.15 with speed
 • SFX: jump, land, roll, coin pickup (pitch rises with combo), powerup pickup, crash, near-miss whoosh
 • Duck music volume 50% during death sequence

Technical Notes for Roblox Implementation
 • All gameplay logic client-side for responsiveness; server validates final score before DataStore write
 • Use RunService.RenderStepped for camera, Heartbeat for movement and collision
 • Tag all obstacles with CollectionService tag Obstacle, coins with Coin, powerups with Powerup
 • Store chunk prefabs in ReplicatedStorage.Chunks
 • Anchor every part in chunks; set CanCollide = false on all obstacles (collision handled by spatial query)
 • Target 60 FPS: keep loaded part count under 2000, use StreamingEnabled on the Workspace


 • Single-player instance per server slot, or separate parallel tracks offset on X by 200 studs for multiple players

answers.ask: The five chunk types are named but not described visually - what should a TrainYard or RampSection chunk actually look like?
answers.answer: Use a bright, colorful cartoon urban subway theme. TrainYard chunks have parallel rails, parked subway trains, signals, and simple platform-side props; BarrierRun is open track with obstacle patterns, TunnelSection is a lit concrete tunnel with overhead signs/low clearance, and RampSection has simple ramps leading onto train roofs or raised track sections.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D endless-runner map in a bright, colorful cartoon urban subway setting, viewed from a third-person camera behind and above the runner. A straight track corridor extends along the +Z axis as repeating 100-stud chunks, with three parallel 8-stud-wide lanes centered at X = -8, 0, and +8. Arrange open track sections, train-yard sections with parallel rails, parked subway trains, signals, and simple platform-side props; barrier-run sections with lane-based barriers and signs; lit concrete tunnel sections with overhead signs and low-clearance overhangs spanning the tracks; and ramp sections that lead onto train roofs or raised track. Place coins in straight lines, arcs, and curved trails above or between the lanes. Keep the track corridor readable ahead, with urban subway structures framing the sides and a clear forward route.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Infinite Runner: the original specifies automatic forward motion through an endless, lane-snapped obstacle path. No secondary genre is needed.

### Shape and preset
Use `lane-snap`, a fixed three-lane subway corridor with the runner shifting between parallel tracks rather than steering freely. This matches the Lane Runner preset; retain its modular chunk and collectible-trail character, while replacing its generic moving-traffic emphasis with the explicitly requested subway-yard, barrier, tunnel, and ramp chunk scenery.

### Config requirements
Use visible `chunk-modular`: repeating 100-stud straight segments align exactly end-to-end along +Z. Use visible `obstacle-jump` for low lane barriers, raised signs, low tunnel clearances, and ramps onto train roofs or raised track. Use `collectible-nodes` as invisible pickup placements, while their coin models remain visibly arranged as straight runs, arcs, and curved aerial trails over and between lanes. No unrequested universal options apply.

### Layout components
Build one infinite straight corridor with three parallel, 8-stud-wide lanes centered at X = -8, 0, and +8. Each 100-stud chunk has a matching entrance and exit cross-section so chunks join without lateral drift. Alternate open track, TrainYard, BarrierRun, TunnelSection, and RampSection chunks without making adjacent chunks visually identical.

Open-track chunks are clear rails with colorful urban retaining walls, support posts, and distant city-subway framing. TrainYard chunks widen visually with parallel rails, parked subway trains, signal masts, platform edges, and simple platform-side props; train roofs can align with ramp approaches. BarrierRun chunks keep the three lane reads clear while placing low barriers, full-height blockers, and raised sign frames in individual lanes. TunnelSection chunks are lit concrete tubes with overhead signs and broad low-clearance overhangs spanning the corridor. RampSection chunks use simple aligned ramps rising from a lane onto a train roof or raised rail deck before returning to the main track. Keep side structures framing the corridor but never obscuring the forward read. Compose from behind and above the runner, with the three lanes converging toward a bright vanishing point.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: draw the authoritative plan first so every modular lane segment, obstacle pattern, ramp connection, and clear continuation is readable and physically continuous before dressing it isometrically.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge because this is an endlessly repeated chunk system rather than a finite course. Theme is bright, colorful cartoon urban subway. Use `P6` because modular obstacle sequences and speed-scaled clearances must remain valid by construction. No additional pipeline modifier is forced.
